en.name: Winter melon
en.summary: Winter melon is the big pale gourd with a waxy bloom on the skin, sold whole or, more often in Taiwan, as a cut wedge. Whole and uncut it belongs in a cool, airy corner of the house, where it keeps about 1–3 months. A cut piece must be wrapped and refrigerated, and lasts about 4–7 days.
en.pantry: A whole winter melon is one of the few vegetables that genuinely stores better out of the fridge. Taiwan's agriculture ministry groups it with bananas, sweet potato, ginger and pumpkin in the 13–15 °C (55–59 °F) class, so a cool, dry, airy corner is right and a cold fridge is wrong. About 1–3 months is realistic for an undamaged melon kept off the floor and out of the sun. The waxy bloom on the skin is what preserves it, so do not scrub it off.
en.fridge: Refrigeration is for cut pieces, which is how most people buy it. Scrape out the seeds and the soft pulp — they are the part that goes first — wrap the cut face tightly in cling film and keep the wedge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below for about 4–7 days. Do not leave the cut face bare; it dries, glazes over and picks up fridge smells. A whole melon should not go in the fridge at all.
en.freezer: There is no freezer timeline for winter melon, and freezing raw chunks is unrewarding: the flesh is mostly water and thaws into a soft, collapsed mass. If you have more cut melon than you can use, the better move is to cook it — a pot of winter melon soup keeps in the fridge for a few days and freezes far better than the raw gourd does.
spoilage: Soft, sunken or weeping spots on the rind of a whole melon
A cut face that has gone slimy, grey or fuzzy with mould
Flesh that has turned translucent and watery instead of firm and white
A sour or fermented smell from the seed cavity
tips: Buy a whole melon with the bloom intact and no bruises; it will outlast any cut piece by a long way.
Keep it off a cold tiled floor and away from direct sun.
Scrape out seeds and pulp before wrapping any cut piece.
Buy cut wedges in the size you will actually cook this week.

faq.q: Does winter melon need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: Not while it is whole. It stores best around 13–15 °C in a cool airy spot. Once cut, it must be wrapped and refrigerated.

faq.q: How long does cut winter melon last in the fridge?
faq.a: About 4–7 days with the seeds scraped out and the cut face wrapped tightly in cling film.

faq.q: How long does a whole winter melon keep?
faq.a: About 1–3 months in a cool, dry, airy corner, as long as the skin is undamaged and the waxy bloom is intact.
There is no timeline for it and raw chunks thaw soft and watery. Cook it into soup instead if you need to keep it.

zh.name: 冬瓜
zh.summary: 冬瓜是表面帶一層白粉的大型瓜，整顆賣，但在台灣更常見的是切塊販售。整顆未切的請放在家裡陰涼通風的角落，大約可放 1～3 個月。切開的一定要包好冷藏，大約 4～7 天。
zh.pantry: 整顆冬瓜是少數「不冰反而更耐放」的蔬菜。農業部把它和香蕉、地瓜、薑、南瓜歸在 13～15 °C 這一類，所以陰涼、乾燥、通風的角落才對，冷冰箱反而不對。沒有損傷、離地、避開陽光的整顆冬瓜，大約 1～3 個月是合理的。皮上那層白粉就是它的保護層，不要刷掉。
zh.fridge: 冷藏是給切開的冬瓜用的，而那正是大多數人買到的形式。先把籽和中間鬆軟的瓜瓤挖乾淨——那是最先壞的部分——切面用保鮮膜緊緊包住，放在 4 °C 以下大約 4～7 天。切面不要裸露；裸放會乾掉結一層膜，還會吸冰箱味。整顆的冬瓜則完全不需要進冰箱。
zh.freezer: 冬瓜沒有冷凍期限，生切塊冷凍也不划算：它幾乎都是水，解凍後會塌成一團軟爛。切太多用不完的話，更好的做法是先煮——一鍋冬瓜湯冷藏可以放幾天，而且比生瓜更適合冷凍。
spoilage: 整顆瓜的外皮出現軟塌、凹陷或滲水的斑點
切面變黏、發灰或長出絨毛狀的霉
瓜肉從結實雪白變成半透明、出水
瓜瓤的部分聞起來發酸或有發酵味
tips: 買整顆時挑白粉完整、沒有碰傷的，會比切塊耐放很多。
不要直接放在冰涼的磁磚地板上，也要避開日曬。
切塊要包起來之前，先把籽和瓜瓤刮乾淨。
買切塊時就買這週真的煮得完的大小。

faq.a: 整顆時不用。它最適合放在 13～15 °C 左右陰涼通風的地方。一旦切開，就必須包好冷藏。

faq.q: 切開的冬瓜放冰箱可以放多久？
faq.a: 挖掉籽和瓜瓤、切面用保鮮膜包緊，大約 4～7 天。
只要外皮沒有損傷、白粉還在，放在陰涼乾燥通風處大約 1～3 個月。
沒有對應期限，生瓜解凍後又軟又出水。要保存的話，建議先煮成湯。
